strengths.I008: Fits position bias, self-preference and discrimination per judge against external verdicts, then spends the fixed vote budget on reliable judges near the top-3 boundary. It costs no extra tokens, needs about 3 days, and can be tested offline by comparing Kendall tau and held-out agreement, uniform vs judge-aware BT. It corrects known judge biases explicitly.
strengths.I006: A bounded repair loop driven by executed check outcomes (FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE rows) rather than critic prose, plus a cross-run template library that a single agent lacks. It targets the development stage, has clean on/off flags, and can be measured by the falsified-claim rate under a held-out checker.

verdicts.reason: I008 directly models and removes position and self-preference bias and is validated against external rankings at no extra token cost, whereas I006 costs about 2x, depends on an unconfirmed check ledger, risks trivially weakened claims, and its final cards show no check text, so the gain may not reach the raters.

strengths.I007: A residual logistic head trained on past blinded verdicts with covariates for length, hedging and family match. It reduces to the current BT ranking when labels are scarce, and it is evaluated by leave-one-brief-out AUC.
strengths.I003: A set-selection rule that maximises the posterior expected best of the 3 delivered ideas, using bootstrapped BT scores and a shared mechanism-cluster shift. It targets the real user need of one good idea, and it corrects a duplication failure that a single agent picking 3 of its own 20 shows. It needs no new generation, only one labelling call per brief, and about 60 lines of code. It can be replayed offline on saved records.

verdicts.reason: I003 improves the selection stage with a concrete mechanism (best-of-3 under correlated same-lever ideas) that is cheap and testable on saved data, whereas I007 needs 15 or more labelled briefs, faces Goodhart risk from panel-derived labels, and is likely to be swamped by brief heterogeneity.
